ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The x(t) in the lower part of the figure is a rectangular pulse, with height 1, and the nonzero interval is from -1 to 1; it is 0 at all other times. The y(t) in the upper part of the figure jumps from 0 to -2 at t=1, then increases along a straight line, reaches 2 at t=5, and crosses zero at t=3; therefore on 1≤t≤5 it can be expressed as y(t)=t-3, where it is negative for 1≤t<3 and positive for 3<t≤5. Reasoning: z(t)=x(t)*y(t)=∫ x(τ)y(t-τ)dτ. Since x(τ)=1 is nonzero only on -1≤τ≤1, z(t)=∫_{-1}^{1} y(t-τ)dτ. Let u=t-τ, then this is equivalent to taking the signed area of y(u) over a sliding window [t-1,t+1] of length 2. In order to make this area maximum, this 2-second window should contain the positive-value part of y(t) as much as possible and avoid the negative-value part. In the figure, the positive-value part of y(t) is exactly from t=3 to t=5, with length 2, so the optimal window is [3,5]. The center of this window satisfies t-1=3 and t+1=5, so t=4. Therefore T1=4 seconds, and rounded to the nearest integer it is still 4.

Compute z(t)=∫_{-1}^{1} y(t-τ)dτ = ∫_{t-1}^{t+1} y(u)du, so z(t) is the signed area under y over a 2-second window. To maximize this area, slide the 2-second window to include as much positive y and as little negative y as possible. The positive part of y is exactly from t=3 to t=5, length 2, so the optimal window is [3,5], whose center is t=4. Therefore T1=4 seconds.

method.method_draft: First extract the graph: x(t) is nonzero only on [-1,1] with value 1, and y(t) is the finite ramp t-3 on [1,5], zero elsewhere. From the problem, z(t)=x(t)*y(t), hence z(t)=∫_{t-1}^{t+1}y(u)du. Differentiate this sliding integral: z'(t)=y(t+1)-y(t-1). For 0<t<2, only the leading edge samples the negative part of y, so z'(t)<0. For 2<t<4, both samples lie on the ramp and y(t+1)-y(t-1)=2>0, so z(t) increases. For 4<t<6, the leading sample is beyond the support while the trailing sample is positive, so z'(t)<0. Thus z(t) changes from increasing to decreasing at t=4; checking support endpoints gives smaller values. Therefore T1=4 seconds.

推理：由卷积 z(t)=x(t)*y(t)=∫x(τ)y(t-τ)dτ。因为 x(τ)=1 仅在 [-1,1] 上非零，所以 z(t)=∫_{-1}^{1}y(t-τ)dτ。令 u=t-τ，可得 z(t)=∫_{t-1}^{t+1}y(u)du，即对 y(t) 做长度为 2 的滑动积分。对 t 求导：z'(t)=y(t+1)-y(t-1)。在 0<t<2 时，t+1 位于 y 的负斜坡部分而 t-1 尚在支撑区间左侧，故 z'(t)<0，z(t) 减小。在 2<t<4 时，t-1 和 t+1 都在斜坡 y(u)=u-3 上，所以 z'(t)=(t+1-3)-(t-1-3)=2>0，z(t) 增大。在 4<t<6 时，t+1 超出 y 的支撑区间右侧，而 t-1 位于正值部分，故 z'(t)<0，z(t) 减小。因此 z(t) 在 t=4 处由增大变为减小，达到最大值。端点处的值较小，所以 T1=4 秒。
